title.narrative: UNU-WIDER Domestic Revenue Mobilisation Program Phase II

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the program is developing countries enabled to improve financing for national development priorities and the SDGs through increased tax revenue and strengthened social contract. The programme is expected to lead to the adoption, implementaion and strengthening of inclusive and equitable development policies, practices and institutions in developing countries, in the area of demoestic recenue mobilisation. These objectives are pursued through enhancing the capacity of target audiences to analyse, design, and implement multiple aspects of research and policies around the themes of domestic resource mobilization. Three broad themes will be in focus in phase II: i) The empirics of tax and social protection, ii) Environmental taxation and just energy transition, and iii) Tax and governance.
Target groups of the program: policy makers and researchers in developing countries, with particular focus on Sub-Saharan Africa. Country specific engagement: Rwanda, Uganda, Zambia, Tanzania, Ghana, Mozambique, South Africa (partnerships with revenue authorities). UNU Wider contributes to tax compliance policies in Zambia's mining sector, and to bridging the gap between research and policy: Tax-benefit microsimulation models, such as SOUTHMOD – developed by UNU Wider, providing country-specific framework to simulate the impact of tax and social benefit policies on different socioeconomic groups. Filling the gap /need for data-driven fiscal policies to ensure effective and equitable tax systems and social protection programmes. Informed policymaking in resource-constrained economies. Moreover, UNU Wider, together with Addis Tax initiative, has developed a Tax Gap Toolkit. Countries like Rwanda and South Africa already having embarked on using the toolkit, and others have expressed interest.
